definition_zh: 婚礼；结婚庆典；结婚纪念
definition_en: a ceremony at which two people marry, and the celebration that follows it
core_image: 一对手挽手从铺满花瓣的门廊走出来，身后是散落的白花和掌声
scene: 院子里的长桌铺着白布，亲戚们从各地赶来，新人从花门下走过时大家一齐起身。 Relatives came from three provinces to the wedding in the courtyard.
sceneCN: 这里 wedding 是「婚礼」（第 1 个义项：两人结婚的仪式与庆典）；句意为亲戚们从三省赶来参加院中的婚礼。手挽手走过花门下、身后落满白花的两人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 婚礼；结婚庆典；结婚纪念

senses.title: The marriage ceremony
senses.definition: the formal ceremony in which two people become husband and wife
senses.definitionCN: 两人正式结为夫妻的仪式
senses.example: The wedding will be held in a small country church.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼将在一座乡下小教堂举行。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the ceremony itself, from the verb wed.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：仪式本身，来自动词 wed。

senses.title: The whole celebration
senses.definition: the party or feast that follows the ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 仪式之后的宴会与庆祝
senses.example: The wedding went on until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼庆典一直持续到半夜。
senses.why: In everyday speech the ceremony and the party blur into one word.
senses.whyCN: 在日常说法里，仪式与宴会合成一个词。

senses.title: A wedding anniversary
senses.definition: used with an ordinal to name a year of marriage, usually silver or golden
senses.definitionCN: 与序数词连用指结婚周年，常见金婚、银婚
senses.example: They are celebrating their golden wedding this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天他们要庆祝金婚。
senses.why: An anniversary repeats the wedding date, so the word for the event names the year too.
senses.whyCN: 纪念日重复的是婚礼那一天，于是事件的词也成了纪年的词。

senses.title: Of or for a marriage
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe things made for a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指为结婚而备的东西
senses.example: She borrowed her sister’s wedding dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她借了姐姐的婚纱。
senses.why: The participle form simply labels objects by the event they belong to.
senses.whyCN: 分词形式只是用所属事件来标记物件。

senses.title: A joining of anything
senses.definition: in literary use, a close union of two ideas, groups or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 在书面用法中指两种理念、团体或品质的紧密结合
senses.example: The design is a wedding of old brick and new glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计是旧砖与新玻璃的结合。
senses.why: Two things joined as closely as a married pair are said to be wedded.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西结合得如夫妻一般，就说它们被「婚配」了。

intro.en: Wedding came from the Old English verb weddian, to pledge, and it once meant the pledge itself rather than the party.
intro.cn: wedding 来自古英语动词 weddian（立誓），起初指誓言本身，而非庆典。

items.en: Weddian meant to pledge or to promise, especially by giving a surety.
items.cn: weddian 意为立誓、许诺，尤指以担保物作保。

items.en: The noun wedding first named the act of pledging and the pledge given.
items.cn: 名词 wedding 最初指立誓的行为与所立的誓约。

items.en: Because a marriage was sealed by a pledge, the word settled on the marriage rite.
items.cn: 由于婚姻以誓约缔结，这个词便固定用于结婚仪式。

items.en: The -ing ending became a plain noun, and the plural weddings appeared.
items.cn: 词尾 -ing 成了普通名词标志，复数 weddings 随之出现。

items.en: Gold and silver wedding extended the word to anniversaries.
items.cn: golden wedding、silver wedding 把词意扩展到结婚纪念。

note.en: The first group is the wedding family, the second the other words for marrying.
note.cn: 第一组是 wedding 词族，第二组是表示结婚的其他说法。

definition_zh: 悲观的；悲观主义的；（估计或预测）偏于不利的
definition_en: expecting bad things to happen, or showing a habit of seeing the worst side of a situation
core_image: 一个人盯着半杯水，眼睛先落在空掉的那一半
scene: 雨还没停，旅店前台的年轻人翻着受潮的地图，把明天的行程一条条划掉。 The clerk was pessimistic about the weather and cancelled every plan.
sceneCN: 这里 pessimistic 是「对……悲观、预感不好」（第 1 个义项：预期坏事会发生）；句意为前台职员对天气不看好，把计划全取消了。图中可辨识物件：受潮的地图、划掉的行程、前台钥匙架。

pos.zh: 悲观的；悲观主义的；偏于不利的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁最高级词干加 -ism 构成，义为「悲观；悲观主义」
由同一词干加 -ist 构成，义为「悲观的人」
由 pessimistic 加 -ally 构成，义为「悲观地」

senses.title: Expecting that bad things will happen
senses.definition: believing that a future situation will turn out badly, and therefore expecting trouble or loss
senses.definitionCN: 相信将来的情况会变坏，因而预期麻烦或损失
senses.example: Investors are pessimistic about next year's profits.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者对明年的利润感到悲观。
senses.why: Latin pessimus is the superlative of bad, so the word starts at the very bottom of the scale: not merely bad, but the worst.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pessimus 是「坏」的最高级，所以这个词的起点在刻度最底端：不是单纯的坏，而是最坏。

senses.title: Habitually seeing the worst side
senses.definition: showing a settled tendency to notice what can go wrong and to expect the least favourable outcome
senses.definitionCN: 表现出一种稳定的倾向：先注意会出问题的地方，并预期最不利的结果
senses.example: He has a pessimistic streak that keeps him from trying new things.
senses.exampleCN: 他性格里有一股悲观的劲头，这让他不愿尝试新事物。
senses.why: A judgement about one future hardens into a temper once it is repeated often enough, so the same adjective can describe a person's outlook rather than a single forecast.
senses.whyCN: 对某件事的预判只要反复出现，就会固化成性情，所以同一个形容词既能描述一次预测，也能描述一个人长期的心态。

senses.title: Casting an estimate in the worst light
senses.definition: describing a figure, estimate, or forecast that is chosen at the gloomy end of the possible range
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个数字、估计或预测落在可能范围中偏坏的那一端
senses.example: The report offers a pessimistic estimate of the repair costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告对维修费用给出了偏高的悲观估计。
senses.why: When a number is picked from the bad end of a range, the adjective moves from the person who expects to the figure that carries the expectation.
senses.whyCN: 当一个数字取自区间的坏的一端，这个形容词就从「做预期的人」转到了「承载预期的数字」上。

intro.en: Pessimistic rests on the Latin superlative for the worst, and the noun behind it was probably coined in French before English borrowed it.
intro.cn: pessimistic 建立在拉丁语表示「最坏」的最高级之上，它背后的名词一般认为先在法语里造出，再传入英语。

items.en: Malus was the ordinary Latin adjective for bad, and its comparative and superlative forms were irregular.
items.cn: malus 是拉丁语里表示「坏」的常用形容词，它的比较级和最高级都是不规则形式。

items.en: Pessimus, the superlative of malus, meant worst, and this one form supplies the root of the whole modern family.
items.cn: pessimus 是 malus 的最高级，意为「最坏的」，现代这一整族词都由这一个形式提供词根。

items.en: Pessimism is generally thought to have been coined in French in the eighteenth century as a name for the view that the world is as bad as it can be.
items.cn: 一般认为，pessimism 是十八世纪在法语里造出的，用来命名「世界已经坏到不能再坏」这种看法。

items.en: English borrowed the noun late in the eighteenth century, first as a philosophical label and only later as the everyday word for gloom.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪后期借来这个名词，先当作哲学标签，后来才变成日常表示消沉的词。

items.en: The adjective adds -istic to pessimist, so pessimistic can describe a person, a mood, or a forecast that carries the same downward pull.
items.cn: 形容词在 pessimist 后加 -istic，于是 pessimistic 既能形容人、形容情绪，也能形容带着同样下坠感的预测。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the pessim- stem and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers words that name gloom or a negative reading of events.
note.cn: 形近组保留 pessim- 词干及其各种词尾；近义组收表示阴郁或对事情作负面解读的词。

entries.definition: The belief that things are as bad as possible or will turn out badly.
entries.definitionCN: 认为事情已经坏到极点或必将变坏的信念。

entries.definition: A person who expects the worst to happen.
In a way that expects the worst.
entries.definitionCN: 以预期最坏结果的方式。

entries.definition: Feeling or showing low spirits, with little hope.
Believing that people act only from selfish motives.
entries.definitionCN: 认为人只出于自私动机行事的。

entries.definition: Focused on faults and drawbacks rather than on what is good.
entries.definitionCN: 着眼于缺点与不利之处而非好的一面。

entries.definition: Offering little hope for the future.
entries.definitionCN: 对未来几乎不抱希望的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin superlative wearing an English adjective ending, so its force is always the bottom of the scale.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语最高级穿上英语形容词词尾，所以它的力度始终在刻度的最低端。

normal.en: Latin pessimus means worst, the irregular superlative of malus, so pessimistic begins at the floor of the scale rather than at bad.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pessimus 意为最坏的，是 malus 的不规则最高级，所以 pessimistic 从刻度的底部开始，而不是从「坏」开始。

normal.en: Pessimist names the person and -ic turns that noun into the adjective, the same way artist becomes artistic.
normal.cn: pessimist 指人，-ic 把这个名词变成形容词，就像 artist 变成 artistic 一样。

normal.en: The usual frame is pessimistic about something: the preposition marks the target of the gloom.
normal.cn: 常见框架是「对某事悲观」，介词标出悲观所指向的对象。

normal.en: A pessimistic forecast is not a sad forecast; it is one that picks the bad end of the possible range.
normal.cn: 悲观的预测不是「伤心的」预测，而是从可能范围里挑了坏的那一端。

normal.en: The word came into English as a philosophical label before it became the ordinary word for expecting rain.
normal.cn: 这个词先以哲学标签的身份进入英语，之后才变成日常里「觉得要下雨」的那种说法。

abstract.en: Picture a glass with the empty half filled in with dark ink: the eye lands there first.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子，空的那一半被深色墨水涂满：目光总是先落到那里。

abstract.en: The stress sits on the middle syllable, so the word itself leans forward toward the worst.
abstract.cn: 重音落在中间音节上，词本身就往前探向最坏处。

abstract.en: A weather app that always shows a storm icon is pessimistic, whatever the sky is actually doing.
abstract.cn: 一个永远显示风暴图标的天气应用就是悲观的，无论天上实际如何。

examples.en: She is pessimistic about the chance of a quick recovery.
examples.cn: 她对迅速复苏的可能性感到悲观。

examples.en: The forecast was pessimistic, but the storm passed us by.
examples.cn: 预报很悲观，但风暴从我们旁边过去了。

examples.en: Years of failed harvests had made the whole village pessimistic.
examples.cn: 连年歉收让整个村子都变得悲观。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕事没戏」——悲观的人遇事总先来一句「怕是没戏」，这就是 pessimistic。

root: 拉丁语 malus（坏的）的不规则最高级 pessimus（最坏的）提供词干，加形容词词尾 -istic；名词 pessimism 一般认为由法语在十八世纪造出。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the worst point of a scale; from it come the expectation that bad things will happen, the temperament that always looks there, and the estimate that is deliberately placed at the bad end.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是刻度上最坏的那一点；由此长出「预期坏事会发生」、「总往那里看的性情」，以及「被特意放在坏一端的估计」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person watching a half-empty glass, with the empty half drawn in dark ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人盯着半杯水，空掉的那一半被涂成深色。

definition_zh: 暗示；提示；迹象
definition_en: a small piece of information that helps you guess or understand
core_image: 雾里露出一点点山尖
scene: 她给了他一个温和的提示。 She gave him a gentle hint.
sceneCN: 这里 hint 是「提示」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她给了他一个温和的提示。

senses.title: Suggestion

senses.definitionCN: 帮助你的一点点建议
senses.example: She gave him a gentle hint.
senses.exampleCN: 她给了他一个温和的提示。

senses.whyCN: 这是表示有用线索的日常义项。

latinIntro.cn: hint 的来源不确定，并非来自拉丁语。

definition_zh: 浅的；浅薄的；浅呼吸的
definition_en: not deep, not showing serious thought, or breathing with little air
core_image: 目光穿过清澈的浅水，直接看到河底的卵石
scene: 孩子们在浅水里玩耍。 The children played in the shallow water.
sceneCN: 这里 shallow 是「浅的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们在浅水里玩耍。

senses.title: Not deep
senses.definition: having only a short distance from top to bottom
senses.definitionCN: 从上到下的距离很短的
senses.example: The children played in the shallow water.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在浅水里玩耍。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Not serious
senses.definition: lacking deep thought or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏深刻思想或感情的
senses.example: The book offers only a shallow view.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书只给出浅薄的看法。
senses.why: Depth of water became a metaphor for depth of mind.
senses.whyCN: 水的深度被隐喻为思想的深度。

senses.title: Light breathing
senses.definition: taking in only a little air
senses.definitionCN: 只吸入少量空气的
senses.example: He was breathing in shallow breaths.
senses.exampleCN: 他在浅呼吸。
senses.why: Each breath goes only a little way down.
senses.whyCN: 每次呼吸只进入很浅的位置。

senses.title: Shallows
senses.definition: an area of shallow water
senses.definitionCN: 水浅的区域
senses.example: The boat stuck in the shallows.
senses.exampleCN: 船搁浅在浅滩上。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for such a place.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为指这种地点的名词。

intro.en: Shallow appears in late Middle English, probably related to Old English words for shoal.
intro.cn: shallow 出现于中古英语晚期，可能与古英语中表示浅滩的词有关。

items.en: Sceald named a shoal or shallow place.
items.cn: sceald 指浅滩或水浅处。

items.en: Schalowe meant not deep.
items.cn: schalowe 意为不深的。

items.en: Shallow described water and containers.
items.cn: shallow 描述水和容器。

items.en: The word described shallow breathing.
items.cn: 这个词描述浅呼吸。

items.en: Shallow became a metaphor for a light mind.
items.cn: shallow 成为思想浅薄的隐喻。

note.en: Shallow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for depth.
note.cn: 把 shallow 与形近词以及表示深度的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shallow means close to the surface, in water, in breath, or in thought.

normal.en: The river is shallow here.
normal.cn: 这里的河很浅。

normal.en: We waded through shallow water.
normal.cn: 我们蹚过浅水。

normal.en: A shallow mind avoids hard questions.

normal.en: His breathing was shallow.

normal.en: The boat grounded in the shallows.

abstract.cn: 浅水容易穿过，也容易看透。

abstract.en: Depth cannot be judged from the surface.
abstract.cn: 深度无法从表面判断。

abstract.en: A shallow answer often ends the question too early.
abstract.cn: 浅薄的回答常让问题过早结束。

examples.en: The children played in the shallow water.

dict_mnemonic.text: shallow 与 shoal（浅滩）同族，核心义「离表面很近」，由水浅引申为思想浅与呼吸浅。

root: 与古英语 sceald（浅滩）相关，核心义「上下距离很短」。

sensesIntro.en: Shallow means not deep in water, breath, or thought, or a shallow place.
sensesIntro.cn: shallow 意为水浅、呼吸浅、思想浅，或浅滩。

core.en: A short distance from surface to bottom.
core.cn: 从表面到底部的距离很短。

branches.en: Water close to its bed.
branches.cn: 离水底很近的水。

branches.en: A mind that stays near the surface.
branches.cn: 停留在表面的头脑。

branches.en: Breath that goes only a little way.
branches.cn: 只进入很浅位置的呼吸。

branches.en: A place where water is shallow.
branches.cn: 水浅的地方。

branches.en: Water and thought share the idea of depth.
branches.cn: 水与思想共享深度的概念。

intro.en: Shallow builds words for degree, manner, and shallow places.
intro.cn: shallow 构成表示程度、方式和浅处的词。

latinIntro.en: Shallow has no Latin ancestor; Latin brevis, short, is only a semantic parallel.

items.example: The shallowness of the pond is visible.

definition_zh: 施加；运用；用力；努力
definition_en: to apply force, influence, or pressure, or to make a great effort
core_image: 双手推开一扇沉重的门
scene: 这家公司向供应商施加了很大压力。 The company exerted heavy pressure on its suppliers.
sceneCN: 这里 exert 是「施加（压力）」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家公司向供应商施加了很大压力。

senses.title: Apply force
senses.definition: to use force, influence, or pressure on someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物施加力量、影响或压力
senses.example: The union exerted pressure on the management.
senses.exampleCN: 工会向管理层施加了压力。
senses.why: Power is pushed outward onto another person or thing.
senses.whyCN: 力量被向外推到别人或别物身上。

senses.title: Try hard
senses.definition: to make a great physical or mental effort
senses.definitionCN: 付出很大的体力或脑力
senses.example: She exerted herself to finish the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她拼尽全力跑完了比赛。
senses.why: The person thrusts effort out from the body.
senses.whyCN: 人把力气从身体里使出去。

intro.en: Exert comes from Latin exserere, to thrust out.
intro.cn: exert 源自拉丁语 exserere，意为向外伸出、使出。

items.en: Serere means to join or put in a row.
items.cn: serere 意为连接或排列。

items.en: Exserere joins ex-, out, with serere.
items.cn: exserere 由 ex-（出）与 serere 组成。

items.en: Exserere means to stretch out or put forth.
items.cn: exserere 意为伸出、使出。

items.en: English exert keeps the image of pushing force outward.
items.cn: 英语 exert 保留把力量向外推的意象。

items.en: Exert pressure becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: exert pressure 成为常用搭配。

note.en: Exert pushes force out; assert states a claim.
note.cn: exert 把力量向外使，assert 则把主张说出来。

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge
to state firmly
great effort
to put force or pressure into use
to force something on others
to make a great effort

normalIntro.en: Exert pushes force or effort outward.
normalIntro.cn: exert 把力量或努力向外使。

normal.en: They exerted pressure on the supplier.
normal.cn: 他们向供应商施加了压力。

normal.en: Parents exert a strong influence on children.
normal.cn: 父母对孩子有很强的影响。

normal.en: The state exerted control over the region.
normal.cn: 国家对这一地区实施控制。

normal.en: He exerted himself to lift the box.
normal.cn: 他用力抬起箱子。

normal.en: Do not exert force on the broken handle.
normal.cn: 不要对损坏的把手用力。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pushing a heavy door.
abstract.cn: 想象双手推开一扇沉重的门。

abstract.en: Imagine a weight pressing down on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个重物压在桌上。

abstract.en: Think of a voice pushing its influence into a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音把影响推进房间。

examples.en: The report exerted strong influence on policy.
examples.cn: 这份报告对政策施加了很大影响。

examples.en: She exerted herself to help the injured man.
examples.cn: 她竭尽全力帮助那名受伤男子。

examples.en: The engine exerts force on the wheels.
examples.cn: 发动机把力施加在车轮上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ ert（使力）」——把力气从身体里使出去，就是施加、用力。

root: 拉丁语 exserere（伸出、使出）＝ ex-（出）＋ serere（排列、连接）→ exert，核心义「把力量向外伸出」。

sensesIntro.en: Exert means to apply force or influence, or to make a great effort.
sensesIntro.cn: exert 意为施加力量或影响，或付出很大努力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pushing a heavy door.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手推开一扇沉重的门。

branches.en: Pushing force onto others is the main sense.
branches.cn: 把力量推向他人是主要义项。

branches.en: Exertion is effort pushed from within.
branches.cn: 努力是从体内使出的力气。

branches.en: Both senses send force outward.
branches.cn: 两个义项都向外送出力量。

branches.en: Influence and pressure are forms of force.
branches.cn: 影响与压力都是力量的形式。

branches.en: The reflexive use stresses personal effort.
branches.cn: 反身用法强调个人努力。

intro.en: Exert combines ex-, out, with Latin serere, to join or put forth.
intro.cn: exert 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 serere（连接、伸出）组成。

latinIntro.en: Exserere becomes exert in English with the same pushing image.
latinIntro.cn: exserere 在英语中变为 exert，保留向外推的意象。

items.exampleCN: overexert 提醒不要用力过度。

senses.definitionCN: 与社会主义或其原则相关的

definition_zh: 举起；抬高；提高（水平、地位）；使（精神）振奋
definition_en: to lift something to a higher position, to raise a level or rank, or to lift someone's spirits
core_image: 一根木杠支在石头上，把沉重的一端缓缓顶起
scene: 工人们用一台旧升降架把石板从坑底吊了上来。 They elevated the beam to the top of the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 elevate 是「举起、抬高」（第 1 个义项：把物体移到更高的位置）；句意是他们把那根横梁吊到了墙顶。

pos.zh: 动词：举起；抬高；提高；使振奋

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「海拔；提升；高地」
由本词的过去分词转作形容词，义为「升高的；高雅的」
由本词加表示施动者的 -or 构成，义为「电梯；升降机」

senses.title: To lift something up
senses.definition: to raise a physical object to a higher place or position
senses.definitionCN: 把实物移到更高处的位置
senses.example: They elevated the beam to the top of the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把横梁吊到了墙顶。
senses.why: Latin levare meant to lighten, and lifting a heavy thing is exactly how you make it feel light, so e- plus levare became to raise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 levare 意为「使变轻」，而举起重物正是让它显得轻的方式，于是 e- 加 levare 成了「举起」。

senses.title: To raise a level or rank
senses.definition: to increase the level, quality or rank of something abstract
senses.definitionCN: 提高抽象事物的水平、质量或地位
senses.example: The new policy elevated the status of rural teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策提高了乡村教师的地位。
senses.why: Height is the oldest picture of importance, so raising a number or a rank borrows the same upward motion.
senses.whyCN: 高度是最古老的表示重要性的图景，于是抬高数字或等级也借用同一个向上的动作。

senses.title: To lift the spirits
senses.definition: to make someone feel happier, nobler or more hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使人更快乐、更高尚或更有希望
senses.example: The music elevated everyone's mood.
senses.exampleCN: 那音乐让所有人的情绪都振奋起来。
senses.why: A low mood is a low position, so cheering someone up is described as lifting them.
senses.whyCN: 低落的心情被看作低处，于是让一个人高兴起来就被说成把他举起。

senses.title: To promote in the church
senses.definition: in religious usage, to raise someone to a higher office, especially in the Catholic Church
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教用法中把某人提升到更高职位，尤指天主教会
senses.example: He was elevated to bishop last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年春天被擢升为主教。
senses.why: An office is a seat placed higher, so appointment to it is spoken of as being lifted up.
senses.whyCN: 职位被想象成摆得更高的座位，因此任命就被说成被举上去。

intro.en: Elevate is Latin e- (out, up) plus levare, to lighten or raise; here the e- really is a prefix from ex-, unlike the e- inside element.
intro.cn: elevate 是拉丁语 e-（向外、向上）加 levare（使轻、举起）；这里的 e- 确实来自 ex- 的前缀，与 element 内部的 e- 不同。

items.en: Levis meant light in weight, the opposite of heavy.
items.cn: levis 意为「轻的」，与「重」相对。

items.en: Levare meant to lighten, and by extension to lift or relieve.
items.cn: levare 意为「使变轻」，引申为举起、减轻。

items.en: Adding ex- gave elevare, to lift out and up.
items.cn: 加上 ex- 构成 elevare，意为「抬出去、举起来」。

items.en: Its past participle elevatus described something already raised.
items.cn: 其过去分词 elevatus 形容已被抬起之物。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century for physical lifting.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，最初指物理上的抬起。

items.en: Rank, mood and church office all took the same upward picture.
items.cn: 等级、心情与教会职位都采用了同一个向上的图景。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the levare family; the near-meaning group separates raise, lift, promote and boost.
note.cn: 形近组收 levare 词族；近义组区分 raise、lift、promote 与 boost。

entries.definition: The machine that lifts people or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电梯；升降机」，即负责举升的机器。

entries.definition: Height above sea level, or the act of raising.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海拔；提升」，指高出海平面的高度或抬起的动作。

entries.definition: Raised up, or noble in style.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升高的；高雅的」。

entries.definition: A bar used to lift; from the same Latin verb levare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杠杆」，与 elevate 同出拉丁语 levare。

entries.definition: The plain everyday verb for lifting; neutral in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「举起、提高」，最日常、语气中性。

entries.definition: To move something up, often with effort and by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抬起」，常指费力地用手举起。

entries.definition: To move someone to a higher job; only the rank sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「晋升」，只对应本词的地位义。

entries.definition: To push a level or mood upward; informal and energetic.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提振、促进」，口语化，强调推力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks take the prefix literally: e- means up, levare means to lighten, so elevating is making heavy things feel light.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把前缀照字面读：e- 是向上，levare 是使轻，所以 elevate 就是让重的东西显得轻。

normal.en: E- is the prefix here, and it means up, out of the way.
normal.cn: 这里的 e- 确实是前缀，意思是向上、抬离原位。

normal.en: Lift a stone and it feels lighter; that is levare in action.
normal.cn: 把石头举起来，它就显得轻了，这就是 levare 在起作用。

normal.en: Elevate a number and it rises; elevate a rank and it climbs.
normal.cn: elevate 一个数字，它上升；elevate 一个等级，它爬高。

normal.en: Good news elevates the mood because joy is pictured as height.
normal.cn: 好消息能 elevate 情绪，因为喜悦被画成高处。

normal.en: Elevator is just elevate plus -or: the thing that lifts.
normal.cn: elevator 就是 elevate 加 -or：负责举升的那个东西。

abstract.en: Picture a lever under a boulder, the far end pressed down.
abstract.cn: 想象一根杠杆压在巨石下，远端被按下去。

abstract.en: The stone rises because the other end was made to feel light.
abstract.cn: 石头升起，是因为另一端被压得「轻」了。

abstract.en: Elevate is the moment when weight stops being the whole story.
abstract.cn: elevate 就是重量不再是全部故事的那一刻。

examples.en: They elevated the beam to the top of the wall.
examples.cn: 他们把横梁吊到了墙顶。

examples.en: The new policy elevated the status of rural teachers.
examples.cn: 新政策提高了乡村教师的地位。

examples.en: The music elevated everyone's mood.
examples.cn: 那音乐让所有人的情绪都振奋起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒维特」——杠杆一压，沉重的石板就离地了

root: 源自拉丁语 elevare，由前缀 e-（＝ex-，向外、向上）加 levare（使轻、举起）构成；levare 出自 levis「轻的」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of elevate: lifting an object, raising a level or rank, lifting the spirits, and promotion to a church office.
sensesIntro.cn: elevate 的四个义项：举起实物、提高水平或地位、振奋情绪，以及教会中的擢升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lever under a boulder, the far end pressed down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根杠杆垫在巨石下，远端被按下去。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: something moved to a higher place.
branches.cn: 实物线：被移到更高处的东西。

branches.en: THE LEVEL: numbers and ranks treated as heights.
branches.cn: 水平线：被当作高度的数字与等级。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: a low mood lifted out of its hollow.
branches.cn: 情绪线：从低谷里被抬起来的心情。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a seat that is higher than the last.
branches.cn: 职位线：比原来更高的一个座位。

branches.en: THE LEVER: the same motion works on stone and on rank.
branches.cn: 杠杆线：同一个动作既作用于石头，也作用于等级。

intro.en: Elevate is e- plus levare; the prefix here is the Latin ex-, meaning out or up, so the e- is genuine and means something.
intro.cn: elevate 是 e- 加 levare；这里的前缀是拉丁语 ex-，意为向外、向上，所以这个 e- 是真正的、有含义的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Levis, levare, elevare and elevatus are all recorded Latin forms; English took the verb through French.
latinIntro.cn: levis、levare、elevare 与 elevatus 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；英语经法语借入这个动词。

items.example: It is the deepest root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族最深的根。

items.example: It gives the English adjective elevated.
items.exampleCN: 它生出英语形容词 elevated。

definition_zh: 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；有多种解释的
definition_en: having more than one possible meaning, or not clear enough to be certain
core_image: 一句话站在两条路口，两条都说得通
scene: 合同里有一句话，双方读出了两种意思。 The wording of the clause was ambiguous, so both sides claimed a victory.
sceneCN: 这里 ambiguous 是「模棱两可的」（第 1 个义项：可以有两种或多种解释）；句意为这一条款的措辞模棱两可，所以双方都宣称自己赢了。

pos.zh: 形容词：模棱两可的；含糊不清的；有多种解释的

derivatives.zh: 由 ambiguous 加 -ity 构成，义为「歧义；模棱两可」
由 ambiguous 加 -ly 构成，义为「含糊地；模棱两可地」
由 ambiguous 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「毫不含糊的」
ambiguity 的复数形式，义为「多处歧义」

senses.title: Open to more than one meaning
senses.definition: able to be understood in two or more different ways
senses.definitionCN: 能够被理解成两种或多种不同意思
senses.example: The sentence is ambiguous because it can mean two opposite things.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以表示两个相反的意思。
senses.why: Latin ambigere meant 'to wander about, dispute', with ambi- 'both' and agere 'drive'; a word that drives both ways is ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambigere 意为「四处游走、争论」，由 ambi-「两边」与 agere「驱动」构成；朝两边驱动的词就是模棱两可的。

senses.title: Not clear or certain
senses.definition: unclear in intention or meaning, so that no firm conclusion can be drawn
senses.definitionCN: 意图或含义不清楚，因而无法得出确定结论
senses.example: His answer was ambiguous, and nobody knew what he wanted.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答含糊不清，谁也不知道他想要什么。
senses.why: The same wandering can be a lack of clarity rather than a double meaning: the hearer cannot fix the word to one point.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「游走」也可以不是双关，而是缺乏清晰：听者无法把这个词固定在某一点上。

senses.title: Of doubtful or mixed status
senses.titleCN: 身份不明的；性质难定的
senses.definition: having a position or nature that is not clearly one thing or another
senses.definitionCN: 所处位置或性质不能明确归为这一类或那一类
senses.example: The project has an ambiguous legal status.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的法律身份不明确。
senses.why: If a thing stands between two categories, it belongs fully to neither, and that in-between state is also called ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物站在两个类别之间，它就不完全属于任何一方，这种中间状态也被称为 ambiguous。

intro.en: Ambiguous comes from a Latin verb for wandering both ways, and its senses keep that image of a word on two roads.
intro.cn: ambiguous 来自拉丁语中表示「朝两边游走」的动词，它的义项保留着「一个词站在两条路上」的意象。

items.en: Ambi- meant 'both, around', the prefix behind ambiguous, ambivalent and ambition.
items.cn: ambi- 意为「两边、周围」，是 ambiguous、ambivalent 与 ambition 背后的前缀。

items.en: Agere meant 'to drive, do, act', the second element of the compound.
items.cn: agere 意为「驱动、做、行动」，是这个复合词的第二成分。

items.en: Ambigere meant 'to go about, wander, dispute', to drive in two directions at once.
items.cn: ambigere 意为「四处走动、游移、争论」，即同时朝两个方向驱动。

items.en: The adjective ambiguus described something that could be taken either way.
items.cn: 形容词 ambiguus 描述可以被理解为任一方向的事物。

items.en: French ambigu carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 ambigu 把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English ambiguous settled in the sixteenth century and later extended to unclear status.
items.cn: 英语 ambiguous 在十六世纪固定下来，后来又扩展到「身份不明」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers unclear and double-edged words.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收含糊与双面类词。

entries.definition: The state of having more than one meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有多种含义的状态。

entries.definition: In a way that can be understood more than one way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以可被多种方式理解的方式。

entries.definition: Having mixed feelings about something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事怀有矛盾情感。

entries.definition: Not easy to understand, without the sense of double meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指不易理解，不带双关意味。

Deliberately open to two interpretations.
Not known or not decided.

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep a word standing at a fork and then turn the fork into unclear status.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子让一个词站在岔口，再把岔口变成不明身份。

normal.en: Ambi means both: ambiguous drives the meaning both ways.
normal.cn: ambi 意为两边：ambiguous 把意思朝两边驱动。

normal.en: A sentence at a fork can be walked down either road.
normal.cn: 站在岔口的句子，两条路都走得通。

normal.en: Ambiguity is the noun for that fork.
normal.cn: ambiguity 就是那个岔口的名词。

normal.en: Unambiguous means the fork has been closed.
normal.cn: unambiguous 意为岔口已被封上。

normal.en: An ambiguous status is a thing standing between two categories.
normal.cn: ambiguous status 就是站在两个类别之间的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a signpost with two arrows pointing opposite ways, both marked true.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌，两个箭头指向相反方向，却都标着「真」。

abstract.en: Now picture a traveller unable to choose, standing still at the post.
abstract.cn: 再想象一个旅人无法选择，站在路牌旁不动。

abstract.en: The stillness of that traveller is what ambiguous describes.
abstract.cn: 那个旅人的静止，就是 ambiguous 所描述的状态。

examples.en: The instructions were ambiguous, so we asked for clarification.
examples.cn: 说明含糊不清，所以我们请求澄清。

examples.en: She gave an ambiguous smile that could mean yes or no.
examples.cn: 她露出一个模棱两可的微笑，可以表示同意，也可以表示不同意。

examples.en: The island has an ambiguous place in the region's history.
examples.cn: 这座岛在该地区的历史中身份不明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必归格斯」——俺必归，格斯却说不清归哪边

root: 拉丁语 ambi-（两边）+ agere（驱动）→ ambigere（四处游走、争论）→ ambiguus（可两解的），经法语 ambigu 进入英语；核心是「一个词朝两边走」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses share one fork: double meaning, missing clarity, and a thing that belongs to neither side.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项共享同一个岔口：双关含义、缺少清晰，以及不属于任何一边的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single word stands at a fork, and both roads can carry its meaning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个词站在岔口，两条路都能承载它的意思。

branches.en: THE FORK: the first sense is a word that fits two readings.
branches.cn: 岔口线：第一个义项是一个词能装下两种读法。

branches.en: THE FOG: the second sense is a word that fits no firm reading.
branches.cn: 迷雾线：第二个义项是一个词无法固定在任何读法上。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the third sense is a thing that sits between two classes.
branches.cn: 边界线：第三个义项是坐在两个类别之间的事物。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE EDGE: both meaning and clarity are split by the same prefix.
branches.cn: 双刃线：含义与清晰都被同一个前缀劈成两半。

branches.en: THE UNFIXED: unclear speech and unclear status share the same stillness.
branches.cn: 未定线：含糊的言辞与不明的身份共享同一种静止。

intro.en: Ambiguous is a Latin adjective with a productive family of noun, adverb and negative forms.
intro.cn: ambiguous 是拉丁形容词，拥有能产的名词、副词与否定形式词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ambi- and agere are the two elements behind ambigere and ambiguus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambi- 与 agere 是 ambigere 与 ambiguus 背后的两个成分。

definition_zh: 感激；感谢；感恩
definition_en: the feeling of being thankful
core_image: 一封写满谢意的信被轻轻折好
scene: 她对老师的帮助充满感激。 She felt deep gratitude for her teacher's help.
sceneCN: 这里 gratitude 是「感激」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她对老师的帮助充满感激。

senses.title: The feeling of thanks
senses.definition: the feeling of being thankful
senses.definitionCN: 心怀感谢的情感
senses.example: She felt deep gratitude for her teacher's help.
senses.exampleCN: 她对老师的帮助充满感激。
senses.why: This is the direct noun for the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接表示这种情感的名词。

senses.title: A lasting thankful state
senses.definition: a settled attitude of thankfulness
senses.definitionCN: 持续而稳定的感恩态度
senses.example: He showed his gratitude with a small gift.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一份小礼物表达感恩。
senses.why: The feeling can become a habit of the heart.
senses.whyCN: 这种情感可以成为内心的习惯。

senses.title: A debt of thanks
senses.definition: an obligation to thank someone
senses.definitionCN: 欠下的人情与谢意
senses.example: We owe him a debt of gratitude.
senses.exampleCN: 我们欠他一份恩情。
senses.why: Thanks are pictured as something owed.
senses.whyCN: 把谢意看作一笔欠下的情。

intro.en: Gratitude comes from Medieval Latin gratitudo, thankfulness.
intro.cn: gratitude 来自中世纪拉丁语 gratitudo，意为感激。

items.en: Gratus meant thankful and pleasing.
items.cn: gratus 意为感激的、令人愉快的。

items.en: Gratia meant thanks and goodwill.
items.cn: gratia 意为感谢与善意。

items.en: Gratitudo named the state of thankfulness.
items.cn: gratitudo 指心怀感激的状态。

items.en: Gratitude entered English as thankfulness.
items.cn: gratitude 以「感激」之义进入英语。

items.en: It became the formal noun for thanks.
items.cn: 它成为表示谢意的正式名词。

note.en: Gratitude is compared with look-alike words and words for thanks.
note.cn: 把 gratitude 与形近词以及表示感谢的词作比较。

entries.definition: feeling thankful
to please
very large or good
the state of being thankful
recognition of value
words of gratitude

normalIntro.en: Gratitude is thankfulness that has learned to stay.
normalIntro.cn: gratitude 是学会留下来的感激。

normal.en: She expressed her gratitude.
normal.cn: 她表达了自己的感激。

normal.en: I feel gratitude for my parents.
normal.cn: 我对父母心怀感激。

normal.en: He wrote a letter of gratitude.
normal.cn: 他写了一封感谢信。

normal.en: Gratitude filled her heart.
normal.cn: 感激充满了她的心。

normal.en: We owe them a debt of gratitude.
normal.cn: 我们欠他们一份恩情。

abstract.en: Gratitude is memory with a warm hand.
abstract.cn: 感激，是带着温度的记忆。

abstract.en: What we thank, we keep.
abstract.cn: 我们感谢的，就会留下。

abstract.en: A thankful heart is never poor.
abstract.cn: 懂得感恩的心，从不贫穷。

examples.en: She felt deep gratitude for her teacher's help.
examples.cn: 她对老师的帮助充满感激。

examples.en: He showed his gratitude with a small gift.
examples.cn: 他用一份小礼物表达感恩。
